summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and functional quadriplegia was admitted with septic shock and respiratory distress. He was found to have ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae and multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, treated with a 7-day course of meropenem followed by cefepime. A vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium urinary infection was covered by linezolid. His sepsis resolved, and he improved clinically with stable vitals and reduced secretions. He was discharged to extended care with plans to complete cefepime, continue oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis, restart citalopram, and follow up with pulmonology.
